answer: A sybil tax prices fake identities out. Each new identity pays a one-time, non-refundable entry fee of 50 POA, so every vertex in the trust graph carries a sunk cost. An attacker minting 1,000 fakes burns 50,000 POA, yet each fake siphons at most ~30 POA before checks catch it — a net loss near 20,000 POA. Honest agents pay once and keep earning rewards; the ocean of cheap copies dries up, since no haven exists for cost-free identities.
